Le `±` est déjà mort dans le code : `handleRefreshControls` ne gère plus que `ctrl+r` et `space`, et `TestTheRefreshIntervalIsNotEditableHere` verrouille ça — seul le libellé dans `GetShortcuts()` a survécu. `space`/Pause-Resume double bien `status.auto_refresh` du tab `status` de `:config`.

Reste `ctrl+r`, où votre raisonnement ne colle pas tout à fait : ce n'est pas un paramètre, c'est une action ponctuelle, et Rule 111 en fait un binding global présent dans toutes les autres vues.

C'est fait — build, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues) et la suite complète passent.

**`internal/ui/status/view.go`**
- `GetShortcuts()` : `±` / *Adjust interval* et `space` / *Pause/Resume* retirés. `ctrl+r` reste.
- `GetHelpContent()` : l'entrée `space` disparaît ; la section *Configuration* renvoie maintenant explicitement à `:config` → tab Status pour l'intervalle et l'auto-refresh.

**`internal/ui/status/update.go`**
- `" "` sort du switch d'`Update()` — la touche est inerte.
- `handleRefreshControls(msg)` → `handleManualRefresh()` : plus de `switch`, plus de toggle. Le commentaire dit pourquoi `ctrl+r` survit — c'est une action, pas un réglage.

**`internal/ui/status/model.go`**
- `paused` → `autoRefresh` (lu tel quel depuis `cfg.Status.AutoRefresh` au lieu d'être inversé). Un champ nommé `paused` sans action de pause mentait sur son seul écrivain ; le nom dit maintenant qu'il vient du réglage.

**Tests**
- `TestSpaceTogglesPause` et `TestResumingAfterTheIntervalChecksImmediately` remplacés par `TestAutoRefreshIsNotToggleableHere` (`space` ne change rien et ne produit aucune commande) et `TestAutoRefreshComesFromTheConfiguration` — le pendant exact de ce qui existait déjà pour l'intervalle.
- `TestHelpDocumentsTheAdvertisedShortcuts` perd son exemption `±`/`?`, devenue morte : les huit raccourcis restants sont tous documentés.

Rien de commité — la branche est toujours `main`, donc dites-moi si vous voulez que je cut une branche + PR.

=== b36176e73e38f1f5e8469e2dd550ddd92e77fcad
docs: record §3.19 — the dashboard stops reflowing, and gains charts (#58)

Two complaints about the dashboard turn out to be one design. It fills in as
its data lands, and it has no live resource metrics.

The reflow is structural rather than incidental. render*Section builds a line
count that depends on state — GitLab is 3 lines loading, 7 loaded, 4 when not
connected; OCI 3 -> 6; Tools 3 -> 2+N — and View() equalises the two columns on
the taller one. So a value landing in the right column moves the left column
too. The rule that fixes it is that a section declares its height and fills it,
which needs three value states where there are two: unknown prints "-",
unavailable prints "n/a" and keeps its labels, zero prints "0". Today "Docker
not available" replaces the whole block, so the user cannot see what the
dashboard would show.

It has a consequence nobody asks for. Once a stale value looks exactly like a
fresh one, the age has to be on screen. m.lastRefresh is stored today and never
rendered; that stops being acceptable.

Everything else was measured on 2026-08-14 rather than assumed, and three
measurements changed the design.

gopsutil's load.Avg() returns {0,0,0} with a nil error on Windows. It does not
fail — it produces a number indistinguishable from data. So load average is
displayed on no platform: a metric present on two of three is worse than one
present on none, because its absence reads as "idle".

docker stats --no-stream costs 1365 / 1982 / 1993 ms against 603 ms for system
df. A 2-second chart tick would keep the CLI running continuously, which is
what forces three clocks instead of the single RefreshTickMsg driving
everything today.

And ntcharts@latest is v2, which requires charm.land/bubbletea/v2 and
lipgloss/v2. A plain go get would drag the whole application into Bubble Tea
v2. The version is v0.5.1, compiled and run against our exact v1 stack.

Bubble Tea v2 is deliberately not bundled with this, and the entry carries the
measured surface so the separate phase does not have to redo the research. The
reason for keeping them apart is one line of it: in v2 msg.String() returns
"space" instead of " ", there are 10 case " ": across 10 files, and the
compiler says nothing because case " ": stays valid Go and simply stops
matching. Rule 135 makes Space the only key allowed to tick a checkbox, so a
careless migration silently breaks every checkbox in the application. That has
to surface in a pull request that does nothing else.

§3.5 asked for braille charts for every container. It becomes a pointer here.
The charts are kept and moved: per-container series belong to the containers
view, where a row is a container, and the dashboard shows aggregates. Its
visual alerts are not carried over — a user-defined threshold is a setting, so
it belongs to the configuration view and needs an entry of its own rather than
a line in this one.

fix: a Docker reference has no scheme (D41) (#53)

§3.8's one open question was whether browsing and pulling can share a URL on a
path-based Nexus. Confirmed by hand against the real instance: they can. A
member needs no third URL, and multiImageName was right to build the pull
reference out of the browse URL.

It was wrong about the scheme, which is what checking turned up. Nothing
stripped http:// or https:// anywhere on the Docker-facing path, so:

  https://registry.example.com             -> https://registry.example.com/api:v1
  https://nexus.example.com/repository/dhi -> https://.../dhi/alpine:3.19

docker pull rejects both. This was never specific to groups — it reached every
registry written with a scheme, which the form does not discourage and which
this package's own doc comments use as the canonical example. Groups only
multiplied it: member URLs are synthesised from the group's, so one scheme in
the config became eight unpullable references.

The same root cause had a second effect that reads as unrelated. The Docker Hub
alias check was a string comparison in three places, so a Hub configured as
https://docker.io matched none of them: normalizeRepoForRegistry withheld the
library/ prefix and every bare image name resolved to a repository that does
not exist.

One helper now answers "what is this registry's host" and one answers "is this
the Hub". registryAPIURL is the single place that still keeps a scheme, and
deliberately: an explicit http:// is how a plain-HTTP registry is reached, so
upgrading it would break that registry rather than fix anything.

Every case in the two new tests fails on the pre-fix code. The existing test
covered only scheme-less URLs, which is why it never said anything.

Renumbered from D39 to D41. This branch was cut before #55 landed, and #55
assigned D39 to a different defect — a discovered group member that browses and
cannot be pulled, still open in §1.3. Two defects held one number until now.

§3.8 is left exactly as #57 rewrote it; only its one sentence naming this
defect is updated to point at D41. The earlier version of this branch also
rewrote §3.8, and that work is superseded.

content.text:
Mergé — [PR #59](https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/59), squash sur `main` en `ec7a4b2`. Local fast-forwardé, branche supprimée des deux côtés (le `-d` a refusé — squash merge, donc pas d'ancêtre commun ; j'ai vérifié `git diff main..branch` vide avant le `-D`).

Le mirror n'a pas laggé cette fois, le `fetch` a rapporté `main` à jour du premier coup.

Deux points sur lesquels j'ai tranché sans vous demander, dites-moi si l'un des deux vous gêne :

- **Pas d'entrée dans `docs/backlog.md`.** Le `±` mort qualifiait honnêtement comme défaut (le header promettait une touche inerte), donc un `D42` en §1.1 aurait été dans la ligne du dépôt — mais ça implique de poser un numéro et de retoucher l'intro « D1 through D38, and D41, are all fixed », et vous n'aviez rien demandé de tel. Le raisonnement est intégralement dans le message de commit. Je l'ajoute si vous voulez.
- **`paused` → `autoRefresh`** dépasse le strict périmètre de votre demande. Justification : sans le toggle, un champ nommé `paused` n'a plus d'action de pause et son unique écrivain est un réglage nommé à l'inverse — le constructeur portait une négation entre le setting et le comportement. C'est une dizaine de sites, tous dans le package.
